Powered by Green Chemistry
A molecule is a small thing. Engineered 
with purpose, it keeps an industry 
cool, seals a system that cannot fail, 
carries current where nothing else 
can. For nearly four decades, this has 
been our work: chemistry applied with 
precision, driven by innovation and 
guided by sustainability, building a 
resilient business on green chemistry, 
operational excellence and deep 
technical expertise.The opportunity before us reaches beyond the products we make. 
Every molecule we develop can enable a smarter technology, a cleaner 
industry, a faster shift to sustainable mobility. That is the transformation 
we are building, and its measure will be the enduring value it creates 
for our customers, partners, communities and shareholders, and the 
sustainable future it powers.Now the same molecules are travelling further. The high-performance chemistry we have always 
supplied to critical industries is becoming the advanced materials of the energy transition, the 
batteries of electric mobility, the systems of energy storage, the technologies of a decarbonising 
world. This is the movement our theme describes: from molecules to mobility, with green chemistry 
as the power behind every step.
We make this journey in balance. Our core businesses stay strong through disciplined execution, 
and their strength funds our investment in high-value, future-ready opportunities. Fluorine 
chemistry and advanced manufacturing remain the expertise beneath it all, placing us where 
science, sustainability and innovation converge. FROM  
MOLECULES TO
MOBILITY

Across nine decades, the INOXGFL Group has built a portfolio that sits on 
both sides of the industrial transition: the chemistry that makes clean 
technology possible, and the renewable energy that puts it to work. 
The Group’s businesses span fluoropolymers, fluorochemicals, battery 
chemicals, wind turbine manufacturing and renewable energy solutions.GROUP PROFILE

RENEWABLE  
ENERGY BUSINESS
CHEMICALS & BATTERY 
MATERIALS BUSINESS
Inox Solar and Inox Solar Americas operate integrated solar PV 
manufacturing platforms in India and the USA. 6 GW of module 
manufacturing capacity is operational, split equally between 
India and the USA, while 8 GW of cell manufacturing capacity 
is under development, comprising 5 GW in India and 3 GW in 
the USA. The vertically integrated platform provides end-to-end 
manufacturing capabilities, improving cost competitiveness 
while unlocking substantial policy-led incentives across India 
and the USA.Inox Solar & Inox Solar AmericasInox Neo Energies is a diversified 
renewable-energy IPP with nearly 8 GW of 
solar, wind, hybrid, FDRE and BESS projects 
in India, catering to utilities, DISCOMs and 
C&I customers through long-term PPAs, 
with a smaller merchant portfolio selling 
power through exchanges. Skypower 
MENA, the group’s African IPP platform, is 
developing a 2.8 GW solar DC portfolio, 
providing the group with a sizeable 
pipeline for growth beyond India.Inox Neo & Skypower MENAInox Clean Energy is an integrated 
renewable-energy platform spanning 
three distinct geographies - India, the USA 
and Africa - with a dual presence across 
renewable IPP power generation and solar 
manufacturing. Its IPP portfolio spans wind, 
solar, hybrid and BESS projects, while its 
manufacturing business covers solar cells 
and modules. The platform has a total IPP 
portfolio of 11 GW, comprising 6.8 GW of 
contracted capacity and 4.2 GW of future 
projects, alongside 6 GW of operational 
module manufacturing capacity and 
8 GW of cell manufacturing capacity 
under construction.Inox Clean Energy Limited

the country’s shift towards sustainable energy.Inox Wind Limited (‘IWL’) – Listed EntityGFCL Solar focuses on producing advanced fluoropolymer

WHO WE ARE
Science, innovation and responsibility have made 
GFL one of the world’s largest and most respected 
names in fluorine chemistry. We combine decades 
of technical leadership with an integrated, 
sustainability-driven operating model to produce 
high-performance fluoropolymers, fluorospecialties 
and refrigerants trusted by customers across the 
US, Europe and key emerging markets.MissionOur

BUSINESS VERTICAL ANALYSIS
We offer a versatile and high-performance 
portfolio of fluoropolymers that enables 
reliability across a broad spectrum of 
downstream applications. As critical 
raw materials, our fluoropolymers 
underpin essential technologies and 
play an indispensable role in the smooth 
functioning of modern industry and society.
Global demand for fluoropolymers is expected to remain robust, 
supported by accelerating adoption across semiconductors, EVs, 
Battery Energy Storage System (BESS), Data Centres for AI and clean 
energy applications 
Demand for high-performance fluoropolymers, including PFA 
and FKM, is expected to outpace the broader market, driven by 
investments in semiconductor fabrication, AI-led data centre 
infrastructure, and next-generation automotive technologies 
The global energy transition is creating new growth avenues, with 
hydrogen, fuel cells, electrolysers and solar technologies expected 
to emerge as significant long-term demand drivers for advanced 
fluoropolymer solutionsDemand Catalysts
OutlookPerformance Snapshot
Electric Vehicles (EVs)
Strong, sustained demand 
for PVDF, PTFE and peroxide-
grade FKM driven by their 
critical use in battery 
components, high-
performance seals and 
advanced insulation systems

CHAIRMAN AND MANAGING DIRECTOR’S STATEMENT
Every molecule we manufacture 
carries a singular ambition: 
to solve challenges that few 
others can. For three decades, 
that ambition has shaped 
our journey, from refrigerants 
that keep industries cool, to 
fluoropolymers that perform 
where conventional materials 
cannot and to chemistry 
engineered with precision, 
patience and purpose.
FY 2025–26 tested that legacy in 
new ways. It was a year marked 
by geopolitical uncertainties and 
volatile markets, with conditions 
shifting with little warning. Yet, 
through this uncertainty, the 
discipline that has shaped our 
chemistry business remained 
our greatest strength, enabling 
us to stay resilient, sharpen 
our execution and continue 
creating value.
Today, that same discipline 
is taking us beyond what 
we have built, towards a 
new chapter of innovation, 
higher-value chemistry and 
sustainable growth.
Because the molecules we 
make no longer stop at the 
factory gate. They are finding 
their way into the batteries 
that will power the next electric 
vehicle, into the membranes 
that will make green hydrogen 
viable, into the materials silently 
enabling a semiconductor fab 
or a solar farm. What began as 
fluorine chemistry for industrial 
problems is becoming fluorine 
chemistry for mobility and 
energy transition itself. Green 
chemistry is the thread running 
through all of it, shaping how we 
manufacture today and what 
we choose to build next.
This year, that ambition 
began to take tangible shape across our businesses. 
We commissioned R-32 
production ahead of schedule, 
strengthening our refrigerants 
business for a world that will 
need cooling more, not less. We 
reached a genuine inflection 
point in battery materials, with 
our integrated LiPF6, electrolyte, 
binders and cathode active 
material platform moving 
from commissioning into 
commercial supply. Through it 
all, our fluoropolymers business 
continued to do what it has 
always done: quietly enable 
industries that cannot afford to 
compromise on performance.
Resilience in a 
Volatile Environment
FY 2025-26 tested the 
industry’s ability to operate 
through uncertainty. US tariff 
policy unsettled the first half; 
geopolitical tensions in the 
Middle East unsettled the 
second. Between them, they 
disrupted global trade flows and 
pushed volatility into commodity 
and currency markets. Little of it 
was within our control.
Yet, volatility of this kind is not 
new to industries built on global 
supply chains. Years like this 
one are what a foundation is for. 
Our diversified portfolio across 
fluoropolymers, refrigerants and 
specialty chemicals gave us the resilience to absorb these 
shocks, while our long-standing 
relationships with customers 
across geographies allowed 
us to maintain continuity and 
trust even as markets moved 
around us.
Operational Agility, 
Disciplined Execution
Resilience alone, however, is not 
a strategy. It must be paired 
with agility. Despite the macro 
headwinds of the year, we 
chose to respond with discipline 
rather than retreat. Across the 
organisation, teams focused 
on stringent cost management 
and sharper execution, ensuring 
that short-term volatility did 
not come at the cost of long-
term direction. This agility 
showed up in the decisions 
we made throughout the year: 
where to prioritise capital, 
which customer relationships to 
deepen and which capabilities 
to build ahead of demand rather 
than in response to it. Discipline 
in the present, conviction about 
the future. Together they turned 
a difficult operating year into a 
year of progress.
Chemistry as the 
Foundation, Green Chemistry 
as the Compass
Green chemistry remains the 
force powering this journey. It 
shapes the way we innovate, 
FY 2025-26 tested the 
industry’s ability to operate 
through uncertainty. US tariff 
policy unsettled the first half;

Fluoropolymers: The Silent 
Enablers of a Structural Shift
We are living through a 
convergence of three 
global trends: sustainability, 
electrification and digitalisation. 
Fluoropolymers sit quietly at the 
centre of all three. Whether it is 
an EV battery, a semiconductor 
fabrication facility, a hydrogen 
electrolyser or a solar 
installation, fluoropolymers play 
a critical enabling role. Their 
combination of thermal stability, 
chemical resistance, dielectric 
performance and durability 
makes them extraordinarily 
difficult to replace in high-
performance applications.
What makes this decade 
significant is the shift from 
niche adoption to large-scale 
deployment. As industries 
accelerate investment in clean 
energy, advanced electronics 
and resilient infrastructure, 
demand for fluoropolymers 
is set to grow not only in 
volume, but also in technical 
sophistication. Four growth 
engines sit before us: electric 
mobility, semiconductors, solar energy and green 
hydrogen. Two of them we find 
particularly compelling over 
the long term. Green hydrogen, 
because fluoropolymers 
are integral to electrolyser 
and fuel-cell membranes 
as decarbonisation targets 
accelerate. Semiconductors, 
because qualifying into high-
purity supply chains brings 
customer integration that is 
deep and durable.
Fluorochemicals: 
Strengthening the Core
While fluoropolymers 
capture much of the 
industry’s imagination, our 
fluorochemicals business 
anchored in refrigerants and 
fluorospecialities remains 
an equally vital part of our 
foundation. We commissioned 
R-32 production, a lower 
GWP refrigerant, well ahead 
of schedule, and are scaling 
capacity to meet rising 
demand from air-conditioning 
penetration, commercial 
refrigeration, cold-chain 
infrastructure and the fast-
growing cooling needs of AI 
data centres. 
Our fluorospeciality 
intermediates continue to 
serve the agrochemical, 
pharmaceutical and electronics 
industries and remain a 
proxy for growth in those 
sectors. Here too, the strategy 
follows the same philosophy: 
back the core business with 
backward integration into 
fluorspar and chloromethanes, 
insulate ourselves from 
commodity volatility and use 
that stability as a platform to 
move into higher-value, more 
sustainable chemistries.

the Next Frontier of Mobility
Fluoropolymers are powering 
the clean-technology era, while Corporation and Middle Eastern

We enter this business with

Innovation, Application, 
and Partnership
Three decades of expertise in 
polymerisation chemistry give

be replicated quickly. But in a 
landscape where customers 
increasingly seek customised 
solutions rather than standard

into application-led innovation. 
Our R&D priorities are focused on 
next-generation fluoropolymers 
for semiconductors, EV batteries, 
green hydrogen technologies 
and advanced membrane

our continued engagement with

collaborative by necessity, 
and we intend to keep building 
bridges between research and 
real-world application.
India’s Opportunity, 
Our Responsibility
As global supply chains diversify 
and companies increasingly

We see both an opportunity and

destination into a genuine 
innovation and development 
hub for specialty materials, 
including fluoropolymers 
and next-generation clean-
energy solutions.

MATERIALITY ASSESSMENT
Understanding the sustainability matters that are most significant to our 
business, stakeholders, people and the environment enables us to focus our 
efforts where they can create the greatest value. During FY 2025-26, Gujarat 
Fluorochemicals Limited (GFL) conducted a Double Materiality Assessment 
(DMA) to identify and prioritise sustainability matters through both impact and 
financial perspectives.
The assessment considers two dimensions: the impact of GFL’s 
activities on people and the environment, and the potential impact 
of sustainability-related risks and opportunities on the Company’s 
financial position, performance, cash flows, access to finance and cost 
of capital. Either perspective can independently establish materiality.
The assessment covered GFL’s manufacturing operations at Dahej, 
Ranjitnagar and Jolva, together with its corporate offices at Noida and 
Vadodara. It also extended beyond the Company’s own operations 
to consider relevant impacts, risks and opportunities across its value 
chain, including raw material extraction, suppliers, procurement 
practices, manufacturing, employees, product safety, distribution, 
customers and end-users.The assessment was aligned with the European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS) and considered 
GFL’s business, value chain, sector developments, peer practices and stakeholder expectations. The 
assessment followed six stages.
The assessment considered GFL’s activities across the upstream value 
chain, own operations and downstream value chain. This included 
raw material sourcing, suppliers, manufacturing, employees, products, 
customers and distribution.Value Chain and 
Assessment Boundary
An initial list of approximately 40 sustainability topics was developed using 
the ESRS sustainability matter framework, chemicals sector considerations, 
relevant industry developments and peer benchmarking. This was 
subsequently consolidated into 12 topics for detailed stakeholder assessment.Identification of 
Sustainability Topics
A structured survey received responses from 127 stakeholders, covering 
Board and Management, investors and lenders, customers, employees, 
suppliers and vendors, regulators and local communities.
The impact materiality assessment comprised 108 respondents, while the 
financial materiality assessment comprised 36 respondents, including Board 
and Management in both cases.Stakeholder 
Consultation
Impact materiality considered the actual and potential positive and negative 
impacts of GFL’s activities on people and the environment across its 
operations and value chain. The assessment considered factors including 
scale, scope, severity and likelihood.Impact  
Materiality
Financial materiality considered sustainability-related risks and opportunities 
that could affect GFL’s cash flows, financial position, financial performance, 
access to finance or cost of capital. The assessment considered both the 
potential magnitude and likelihood of the financial effect.Financial  
Materiality
Responses were consolidated separately for the two materiality 
lenses, with stakeholder-specific weightages applied to reflect the 
relevance of different stakeholder groups. Each topic received an 
impact materiality score and a financial materiality score, with the 
topics ranked based on the higher of the two scores.Consolidation and 
PrioritisationDouble Materiality Assessment Methodology

finance or cost of capital.Why Both Lenses

STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT
Every stakeholder contributes something 
essential to our progress. Consistent, meaningful 
engagement gives us the insights that shape 
our decisions, strengthen our relationships and 
reinforce our shared purpose. Our approach rests 
on transparency and responsiveness: we listen,

Stakeholder Engagement Process
Plan and Design
We define the purpose, scope and priorities of engagement to align with organisational 
goals. A clear roadmap and stakeholder map guide how and where we focus our efforts.
Prepare and Assign
Roles, responsibilities and cross-functional teams are established to drive the engagement 
agenda. Internal alignment creates a unified and informed approach.
Consult, Synthesise and Strategise
We collaborate with stakeholders to refine priorities and co-develop actionable strategies. 
Inputs are synthesised into clear plans that balance expectations with business imperatives.
Build, Commit and Implement
Agreed strategies are translated into targeted initiatives with clear timelines and ownership. 
Organisation-wide commitment ensures consistent execution and visible progress.
Monitor, Evaluate and Report
Ongoing monitoring tracks performance against expectations, enabling timely course 
corrections. Regular reporting reinforces transparency and demonstrates accountability.Listen and Engage 
We gather insights through dialogues, surveys and interactions to understand expectations 
and emerging issues. This ensures every stakeholder voice is heard and valued.
Build Trust through Strategic Review
Key insights are analysed to identify opportunities, risks and focus areas. Transparent 
sharing of findings strengthens trust and credibility with stakeholders.

our natural graphite anode

long-term manufacturing 
footprint and global

Manufacturing Strength that Begins with 
Integration
One of our strongest competitive advantages lies 
in our integrated manufacturing ecosystem, which 
connects multiple stages of the fluorochemical value 
chain into a unified operating platform. This integration 
enables us to optimise manufacturing across product 
families, improve resource utilisation and build resilience 
against demand fluctuations and external disruptions. 
We have strengthened this network year after year 
through improvements in raw material consumption 
norms, expansion of captive production capacity and 
deeper process integration. These steps have reduced 
dependence on external markets for critical intermediates, 
improved cost visibility and given us tighter control over 
production economics.

through Backward Integration
Backward integration remains a 
foundation of our manufacturing strategy.
A large proportion of our critical raw 
materials is produced in-house, leaving 
little dependence on external markets 
beyond a few commodity inputs such 
as coal and salt. This gives us greater 
control over raw material availability, 
product quality and manufacturing costs 
and reduces exposure to global supply 
disruptions and price volatility. For high 
performance fluorochemicals and battery 
materials, where product consistency 
and purity are critical for customer 
qualification, backward integration is a 
distinct competitive advantage. It ensures 
reliable access to critical intermediates 
and strengthens supply assurance for 
customers operating in highly regulated 
and technology intensive industries.Ranjitnagar,

Aligning Our Manufacturing Footprint 
for Future Growth
As market demand shifts towards advanced 
materials and sustainable technologies, we continue 
to realign our manufacturing footprint for the next 
phase of growth. Investments in debottlenecking, 
capacity expansion, process optimisation and 
selective retrofitting are enabling our facilities to 
manufacture a broader portfolio of high-value 
products while preserving operational flexibility 
across legacy businesses.
Our manufacturing transformation has one aim: 
to raise the contribution of fluoropolymers and 
battery materials without compromising the 
efficiency of refrigerants and bulk chemicals. Existing 
assets are upgraded to support new chemistries, 
improve process capability and accelerate 
commercialisation of advanced products. 
This balance lets us capture emerging growth 
opportunities while managing market cyclicality 
across traditional product segments.Scaling Capacity to Expand 
Possibilities
During the year, we continued to strengthen 
our manufacturing platform through targeted 
capacity additions and process optimisation 
that improved operational flexibility and the 
product mix.
Commissioned additional R-32 production 
capacity at the existing refrigerants 
facility, strengthening our next-generation 
refrigerant portfolio and supporting 
evolving environmental regulations.
Achieved 3ABTF production of 100 MT per 
month, improving capacity utilisation 
and strengthening downstream 
fluorochemicals manufacturing.
Building the Manufacturing Backbone for 
Battery Materials
Our existing infrastructure continues to evolve towards 
next generation battery chemistries through selective 
retrofitting and technology-led upgrades. 
These electrolyte additives are critical to the safety, 
performance and cycle life of lithium-ion batteries. The 
ability to leverage existing infrastructure while introducing 
advanced chemistries demonstrates the flexibility and 
scalability of our manufacturing platform.During the year, we commissioned 
facilities for the production of Vinylene 
Carbonate (VC) and Fluoroethylene 
Carbonate (FEC) at our Ranjitnagar plant. 
Customer samples have already been 
supplied for qualification, an important 
milestone in the commercialisation of our 
battery materials portfolio.Driving Operational Excellence 
through Asset Optimisation
During the year, focused process improvement 
programmes delivered measurable gains in 
manufacturing efficiency, reducing raw material 
consumption, improving yields and enhancing 
cost competitiveness, all without significant 
incremental capital investment.Building Reliability into Every Operation
Reliable assets are essential to consistent product 
quality and dependable customer service. During 
the year, continuous reliability programmes 
strengthened equipment availability, improved plant 
performance and steadied operational performance 
across  facilities. Preventive maintenance, predictive 
monitoring and process discipline continue to 
minimise downtime. These disciplines underpin our 
ability to meet customer commitments consistently 
while improving manufacturing efficiency over the 
long term.
Manufacturing Close to Global 
Customers
As our portfolio evolves towards advanced 
fluorochemicals, fluoropolymers and battery 
materials, our manufacturing base is increasingly 
supported by an expanding international network. 
Regional warehouses and international offices 
bring us closer to customers, improving regional 
fulfilment and reducing delivery lead times. The result 
is faster servicing, stronger supply assurance and 
closer technical collaboration with global OEMs and 
advanced material manufacturers. The network also 
deepens our participation in rapidly expanding global 
value chains, across electric mobility, energy storage, 
semiconductors and clean technologies, while 
reducing concentration risk and improving supply 
chain resilience.Our Globally Recognised Certifications

Patent Portfolio Development
We actively identify patentable innovations from R&D, 
process development, engineering improvements 
and manufacturing practice. Every incremental 
and meaningful invention undergoes systematic 
evaluation for novelty, inventive step, commercial 
applicability and freedom-to-operate (FTO) 
before filing decisions are made. Patent protection 
is pursued across India and key international 
jurisdictions, in line with business priorities, 
commercialisation plans and market opportunities.
Patent portfolio reviews, prior-art searches, 
patentability assessments, FTO studies and 
competitive intelligence are undertaken 
regularly to strengthen our innovation pipeline, 
minimise infringement risks and reinforce our 
competitive advantage.
Brand Protection 
and Commercial 
Safeguards
Beyond technology, 
we protect the value 
of our brands and 
commercial assets 
through comprehensive 
Trademark management 
and contractual controls. 
Our trademarks are 
monitored continuously to 
detect unauthorised use, 
infringement or dilution, 
while legal enforcement 
mechanisms safeguard 
brand reputation and 
market recognition. 
Intellectual property 
ownership, confidentiality 
obligations and non-
disclosure provisions 
are embedded across 
employment contracts, 
technology partnerships, 
licensing arrangements, 
research collaborations 
and supplier agreements, 
keeping Company-
developed innovations 
protected throughout the

Enterprise
Digitalisation is transforming the way we manufacture. We are progressively 
integrating automation, advanced analytics and real-time monitoring into 
our manufacturing operations to improve operational visibility, strengthen 
process reliability and accelerate decision-making. The year’s milestone was 
the implementation of SAP S/4HANA, a unified digital platform integrating 
procurement, production, inventory, maintenance and enterprise-wide 
operations. Real-time information means faster planning, better coordination 
and more informed decisions across facilities. Around it, a growing suite of 
Industry 4.0 technologies is strengthening manufacturing intelligence.
Digital Security for Intellectual Capital
As digital technologies become more deeply embedded 
across our operations, cybersecurity becomes inseparable 
from protecting intellectual capital. A secure digital 
architecture integrates cybersecurity across IT, OT and cloud 
environments to safeguard proprietary designs, research 
outputs, manufacturing data and critical business information. 
Identity and Access Management (IAM), role-based access 
controls, multi-factor authentication and Zero Trust principles 
ensure that sensitive information reaches only to authorised 
personnel. Advanced Data Loss Prevention (DLP) systems, 
secure collaboration platforms and controlled information 
management minimise the risk of unauthorised access, 
disclosure or data leakage.
Key Capabilities Include
 AI-enabled security operations supported by 
continuous monitoring and predictive threat 
intelligence 
 Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) 
and Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR/XDR) 
 DevSecOps practices integrating automated security 
testing throughout software development 
 OT/ICS security controls including network 
segmentation, anomaly detection and monitoring of 
critical manufacturing assets 
 24×7 Security Operations Centre (SOC) with proactive 
incident detection and response 
 Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery 
frameworks supporting operational resilience Our cybersecurity 
framework aligns 
with internationally 
recognised standards, 
including ISO/IEC 
27001, ISO/IEC 42001, 
the NIST Cybersecurity 
Framework, and 
complies with the Digital 
Personal Data Protection 
(DPDP) Act, supporting 
secure, compliant and 
responsible digital 
adoption.
Building an 
Innovation-led Culture
Intellectual capital begins 
with people. Employees are

Regular cybersecurity

information management and 
minimise human-related risks.

Business Practices
Respect for human rights is embedded throughout

Zero Tolerance 
towards Child Labour
GFL strictly prohibits the 
employment of children under 
any circumstances.
Our recruitment process 
includes mandatory 
verification of age through 
valid government-issued 
documents to ensure 
compliance with applicable 
labour laws, the United 
Nations Convention on the

ILO Convention No. 182.

The Company maintains a firm commitment to eliminating every form 
of forced, bonded, compulsory, or involuntary labour.
Our employment practices are designed to safeguard individual 
freedom and comply with the principles laid down under ILO 
Conventions 29 and 105.
Working hours are regulated in accordance with the provisions of 
the Factories Act, 1948, with employees working standard shifts and 
receiving statutory overtime compensation wherever applicable.
To reinforce ethical workplace practices, all employees and 
contract workers undergo regular awareness programmes covering 
business ethics, workplace conduct, and Prevention of Sexual 
Harassment (POSH).

At Gujarat Fluorochemicals Limited (GFL), Corporate Social Responsibility is an extension of our belief that 
long-term business success must be accompanied by meaningful social progress. Our approach goes 
beyond philanthropic interventions to create sustainable, community-led development that strengthens 
livelihoods, improves access to essential services, enhances environmental resilience and enables people to 
build better futures. The Company’s CSR philosophy focuses on creating lasting value through programmes 
that address local priorities while contributing to national development and the United Nations Sustainable 
Development Goals. 
During FY 2025-26, our interventions reached thousands of beneficiaries across education, healthcare, 
livelihoods, women empowerment, sustainable agriculture, water conservation, environmental stewardship 
and community infrastructure. Each programme has been designed to address root causes, strengthen 
local capacities and deliver measurable, long-term outcomes rather than one-time support.Empowering Communities. Enabling Sustainable Futures.

Economic empowerment lies at the heart of resilient 
communities. GFL’s livelihood initiatives focus on creating 
sustainable income opportunities by combining skill 
development, enterprise creation and market access. Rather 
than limiting interventions to vocational training, the Company 
has built an integrated ecosystem that enables beneficiaries,

The Skill Development Centre provides free, demand-driven 
training in tailoring, embroidery, jute bag making, resin

market opportunities.

exposure and opportunities to generate sustainable 
incomes while balancing household responsibilities. Through 
participation in exhibitions, institutional orders, digital sales 
channels and linkages with government livelihood schemes 
such as Hastakala Setu, Vishvakarma Yojana and the National 
Rural Livelihood Mission, artisans are able to access wider 
markets and strengthen their entrepreneurial capabilities.

community development.

schemes and organised awareness programmes on health, hygiene and menstrual well-being. Swasthya 
Sakhi Kits were distributed to adolescent girls, while community outreach through Anganwadis and 
International Women’s Day celebrations encouraged greater participation and recognition.

Access to quality healthcare remains a significant challenge for many 
rural communities. Through the SWASTHYAM Mobile Healthcare Unit, 
GFL continued bringing healthcare services directly to underserved 
villages, reducing barriers to timely diagnosis and treatment.
The programme combines mobile medical consultations, medicine 
distribution and preventive healthcare awareness with specialised 
screening camps covering eye health, X-rays, anaemia and menstrual 
hygiene. By integrating awareness with treatment, the initiative 
promotes healthier lifestyles while reducing the financial burden on 
rural households.
Agriculture remains the primary livelihood for many families 
surrounding our operations. GFL supports farmers by promoting 
sustainable farming practices that improve productivity while 
reducing dependence on chemical inputs.
Through expert advisory services, field demonstrations and structured 
training programmes, farmers receive practical guidance on organic 
farming, soil health improvement, vermicomposting, composting 
techniques and the use of natural fertilisers such as Jeevamrut 
and Panchagavya.
Animal husbandry plays an important role in supporting rural incomes. 
GFL’s integrated programme combines doorstep veterinary care, 
emergency dairy coupon support and farmer training to improve 
livestock health and productivity.
Qualified veterinary professionals provide regular village visits, 
disease diagnosis, vaccination support and guidance on nutrition, 
breeding and livestock management. Emergency veterinary services 
further ensure timely treatment, helping reduce livestock losses while 
improving milk productivity and farmer incomes. 9,558

Managing Environmental Performance 
Systematically
Environmental sustainability is embedded into our operations 
through structured systems, clearly defined responsibilities and 
continuous performance monitoring. Integrated Management 
System (IMS) provides a unified framework for identifying 
environmental aspects, assessing risks and implementing mitigation 
measures across all manufacturing locations.
Our Environmental Management Systems are certified to ISO 14001 
standards and supported by periodic internal audits, environmental 
monitoring, data-driven decision-making and continual 
improvement programmes. Dedicated environmental teams 
work closely with operational functions to ensure environmental  
considerations are integrated into production planning, 
maintenance activities and capital investment decisions.
Environmental performance is reviewed regularly by senior 
leadership through structured governance mechanisms, ensuring 
timely corrective actions, knowledge sharing and continuous 
enhancement of environmental performance across the 
organisation. 
Our Environmental Governance Framework
Strong governance remains central to our ability to manage environmental impacts effectively while 
responding proactively to emerging sustainability challenges. During the year, we further strengthened 
our governance architecture by establishing dedicated sustainability committees and integrating 
climate-related considerations more deeply into enterprise-wide decision-making.

Climate Scenario 
Analysis
To understand potential 
long-term impacts of climate 
change, GFL undertakes 
scenario analysis using climate 
projections referenced in IPCC 
AR5 and AR6 literature. Multiple 
Representative Concentration 
Pathway (RCP) and Shared 
Socioeconomic Pathway (SSP) 
combinations are assessed 
to evaluate changes in 
temperature, precipitation 
and water stress up to 2030 
and 2050, helping strengthen 
resilience under varying climate 
futures. Climate Scenario Description Purpose
Strong global decarbonisation  
and rapid emissions reductionOptimistic  
(RCP 2.6/SSP1)Evaluates resilience under  
a low-carbon transition
Business-as-Usual  
(RCP 4.5/SSP2)Moderate emissions with  
gradual policy actionRepresents the most likely  
transition pathway
High Emissions  
(RCP 8.5/SSP5)Limited mitigation and  
continued emissions growthAssesses resilience under  
severe climate impacts
This scenario-based approach enables GFL to evaluate both 
operational vulnerabilities and emerging opportunities while 
supporting long-term capital planning and investment decisions.

Engineering a Lower-Carbon FutureEnergy Optimisation Initiatives
At GFL, we are committed 
to building a greener and 
more sustainable future by 
strengthening manufacturing 
performance while responsibly 
managing our environmental 
footprint. Through integrated 
operational synergies, we 
enhance efficiency, drive 
innovation, and reinforce our 
commitment to reducing both 
direct and indirect greenhouse 
gas (GHG) emissions. In FY 
2025-26, our Scope 1 and 
Scope 2 emissions amounted 
to 7,13,632 tCO2e. Reflecting the 
success of our decarbonisation 
initiatives, we achieved a 27% 
YoY reduction in GHG emissions intensity, decreasing from  
1.62 tCO2e/MT in FY 2024-25 to 
1.26 tCO2e/MT in FY 2025-26.
As part of our ongoing 
commitment to climate 
action and a greener planet, 
we are accelerating the 
adoption of renewable energy 
across our operations. This 
strategic transition has 
significantly reduced our 
Scope 2 emissions. Emissions 
from purchased electricity 
decreased significantly by 
55%, from 2,29,308 tCO2e in 
FY 2024-25 to 1,02,724 tCO2e 
in FY 2025-26, demonstrating 
meaningful progress towards our decarbonisation goals  
and long-term 
sustainability ambitions.
Alongside these efforts, we 
expanded the use of renewable 
energy to reduce dependence 
on conventional power sources 
and support our long-term 
decarbonisation roadmap.
Together, these initiatives reflect 
our approach of combining 
engineering excellence with 
responsible resource utilisation 
to build a manufacturing 
network that is efficient, resilient 
and future-ready.

Product Stewardship
Our responsibility extends beyond manufacturing operations to 
the products we develop. We continue to integrate sustainability 
considerations into product design through Green Chemistry 
principles, enabling products that balance performance with lower 
environmental impacts.
Life Cycle Assessments (LCA), conducted in accordance with ISO 
14040 and ISO 14044 standards, evaluate environmental impacts 
across each stage of a product’s lifecycle. These assessments 
support process improvements, identify opportunities to optimise 
resource use and strengthen environmental performance.
Complementing this approach, Product Carbon Footprint (PCF) 
assessments quantify product-level greenhouse gas emissions, 
providing customers with greater transparency and supporting 
the management of Scope 3 emissions across their value chains.

Circular Resource Management
During the reporting year, GFL successfully modified the caustic 
flaker heating system to replace natural gas with by-product 
hydrogen generated from the Chlor-Alkali electrolysis process. 
Necessary burner modifications, fuel management systems, 
safety controls, and operational optimisations were implemented 
to enable the efficient utilisation of hydrogen fuel without 
affecting production performance or product quality.
This initiative created a closed-loop energy solution, converting 
an internally available by-product into a valuable energy 
resource while reducing reliance on fossil fuels.Our manufacturing processes 
are designed to maximise the 
productive use of resources 
by recovering, recycling 
and reusing materials 
wherever technically and 
economically feasible. This 
approach not only reduces 
waste generation but also 
improves resource efficiency 
and supports responsible 
manufacturing practices.The Company continues to 
strengthen circularity through 
process improvements that 
enhance by-product recovery, 
increase material reuse and 
optimise waste handling across 
manufacturing operations. 
Engineering interventions 
and operational controls help 
minimise waste generation 
at source, while approved 
recycling and co-processing

ECONOMIC OVERVIEW
GLOBAL ECONOMIC OVERVIEW
Global growth is estimated at 3.4% in 2025, with a slight 
moderation to 3.1% in 2026 before stabilising at 3.2% in 
2027. This reflects a phase of steady expansion, supported 
by easing inflation and sustained investments in technology, 
even as trade policy uncertainties and evolving geopolitical 
dynamics continue to shape the broader economic 
landscape. Despite ongoing global challenges, growth 
remains resilient, supported by policy measures and 
continued momentum in private sector investment.
The prolonged Russia-Ukraine conflict continued to unsettle 
energy markets, commodity flows, and agricultural trade, 
particularly affecting Europe’s energy dynamics. The Middle 
East witnessed escalating tensions since late February, with 
conflict around Iran disrupting shipping through the Strait 
of Hormuz and raising concerns over other critical trade 
corridors, including Red Sea routes. Meanwhile, strategic 
rivalry between the United States and China resulted in tariff 
wars, tighter technology controls, and competition over 
critical minerals. This accelerated supply chain restructuring 
through friend-shoring and near-shoring strategies.
Beyond major power rivalries, instability across several 
emerging markets is compounding pressures on global 
trade, investment, and capital flows. Sanctions are changing 
trade dynamics, increased defence expenditure is redefining 
priorities, and shifting global alliances are reshaping 
engagements. In this environment, businesses are promptly 
evaluating their sourcing models, investment strategies, and 
long-term geographic exposure. Moreover, the realignment 
of geopolitical landscape is driving economies to boost 
domestic manufacturing capabilities, expand clean energy MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION AND ANAL YSIS REPORT
initiatives, strengthen electric mobility ecosystems, and 
accelerate digital infrastructure, as new trajectories evolve 
for medium-term growth.
As these dynamics unfold, the global growth trend reveals 
increasing regional divergence. In advanced economies, it is 
expected to remain moderate, supported by targeted fiscal 
measures and sustained spending on digital and technology 
infrastructure. Europe, meanwhile, is showing signs of relative 
stability, helped by stronger public expenditure, particularly 
in Germany, and resilient performance in countries such as 
Ireland and Spain. A close look at the emerging market and 
developing economies reveals sustained policy impetus 
across selected markets, coupled with reform-led growth 
and improving macroeconomic stability. However, structural 
challenges continue to weigh on the growth prospect of 
some economies from this block.
With these divergent trajectories shaping the global 
outlook, a gradual moderation in inflation presents a silver 
lining. Headline inflation is estimated to decline from 
4.1% in 2025 to 3.8% in 2026 and further to 3.4% in 2027, 
reflecting softer commodity prices and easing supply-side 
pressures. Energy prices are expected to remain volatile 
in the near term, influenced by geopolitical developments, 
supply dynamics, and shifts in global demand. While some 
moderation in overall energy costs may be observed, a sharp 
decline appears unlikely. Oil prices are expected to remain 
range-bound with intermittent fluctuations, reflecting 
ongoing macroeconomic uncertainties and evolving supply 
conditions. Although trade barriers, geopolitical tensions, 
and policy uncertainty may affect near-term sentiment, their 
drag on growth is expected to gradually soften, supporting a 
more stable macroeconomic environment over the coming 
years.

PERFORMANCE OF MAJOR ECONOMIES IN 2025
The United States
The United States economy demonstrated continued 
resilience in 2025, with real GDP growth estimated at around 
2.8%, supported by robust consumer spending, easing 
financial conditions, and sustained investment activity. 
According to the IMF’s April 2026 World Economic Outlook, 
growth is expected to moderate to 1.9% in 2026, reflecting 
the lagged impact of tighter monetary policy, softer 
consumption momentum, and evolving trade dynamics. 
While inflationary pressures have eased compared to prior 
years, they remain above target, prompting a cautious 
and data-dependent policy stance by the Federal Reserve. 
Labour market conditions have gradually softened, although 
they continue to remain relatively strong, supporting overall 
economic stability.
Euro Area
The Euro area recorded subdued growth of approximately 
0.8% in 2025, as economic activity remained constrained 
by weak industrial output, elevated energy costs, and 
lingering geopolitical uncertainties. The IMF projects a 
modest recovery to 1.5% in 2026, supported by improving 
real incomes, gradual monetary easing, and a stabilisation 
in energy markets. However, structural headwinds including 
weak productivity growth, cautious business sentiment, and 
uneven fiscal support across member states, continue to 
weigh on the pace of recovery, keeping the growth outlook 
moderate.
China
China’s economy expanded by around 4.8% in 2025,  
reflecting the combined impact of policy stimulus, 
infrastructure investment, and targeted support measures. 
As per the IMF’s April 2026 outlook, growth is expected to 
moderate further to 4.5% in 2026, as structural challenges 
persist. These include subdued domestic demand, ongoing 
stress in the property sector, and demographic headwinds. 
While policy support and external trade stability may provide 
some cushioning, China’s growth trajectory continues to 
shift towards a more consumption-driven and sustainable 
model, albeit at a slower pace.
(Source: https://www.imf.org/en/publications/weo/
issues/2025/04/22/world-economic-outlook-april-2025 )
Outlook
While the global growth outlook remains broadly stable, 
several downside risks remain. Escalating trade tensions, 
persistent geopolitical uncertainty, and high public debt 
could tighten financial conditions and weigh on economic 
activity. In addition, if expected productivity gains from AI-led investments fall short, markets may become more 
volatile, while business and investor sentiment may weaken.
Growth may also be limited by structural constraints, with 
uneven sectoral and regional distribution of technology-
driven benefits adding to the drag. In this context, 
policymakers stay focused on accelerating structural 
reforms, rebuilding fiscal buffers, preserving price and 
financial stability, and reducing uncertainty to support long-
term growth.
(Source: https://www.imf.org/en/publications/weo/
issues/2025/04/22/world-economic-outlook-april-2025 )
INDIAN ECONOMIC OVERVIEW
Positioned as a key driver of global growth, India registered 
a nominal GDP growth of 7.7% in FY 2025-26, marking its 
fourth consecutive year as one of the fastest-growing major 
economies. This growth momentum is driven by domestic 
demand, led by private consumption, which accounts for 
61.5% of GDP , as per the First Advance Estimates by the 
National Statistical Office, further supported by sustained 
investment activity.
Rural demand is emerging as a key driver of this momentum, 
with a NABARD survey confirming stronger consumption 
growth in rural India compared to urban areas. A normal 
monsoon, improved agricultural output, easing inflation, easy 
accessibility of credit, and supportive government measures 
are driving this trend. The survey also suggests a significant 
rise in rural household spending, with a large share of 
income directed towards consumption of goods, services, 
and durables, alongside a noticeable shift towards non-farm 
income sources. This reflects a structural transformation, 
with rural India evolving from a supply-side contributor into 
an increasingly important consumption hub.
This sound consumption landscape is supported by a 
favourable macroeconomic environment, characterised by 
low inflation, stable employment conditions, and rising real 
incomes. Healthy agricultural output and a gradual recovery 
in urban demand are further strengthening consumption, 
supported in part by tax rationalisation measures. Buoyed 
by these factors, domestic economy remained resilient in 
the midst of a volatile global environment shaped by trade 
disruptions, tariff pressures and capital flow uncertainty.
Investment activity also remained robust, with Gross Fixed 
Capital Formation estimated at 30% of GDP , reflecting 
continued confidence in the economy’s medium-term 
prospects. This momentum stems from sustained public 
capital expenditure, ongoing infrastructure creation, 
and improving private sector sentiment, fortifying the 
investment cycle. A growing share of this investment is 
being directed towards renewable energy infrastructure, MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION AND ANAL YSIS REPORT (CONTD.)Corporate Overview Statutory Reports Financial StatementsGujarat Fluorochemicals Limited

solar capacity expansion, and EV ecosystem development, 
accelerating India’s transition towards a sustainable, 
future-ready economy. This is further supported by a stable 
macroeconomic environment, characterised by fiscal

and continued structural reforms.

economic activities in India.

expenditure prioritisation enabled the government to support 
capital formation and social spending, while maintaining 
fiscal prudence. This balanced approach boosted confidence 
in the broader economic framework.
Monetary policy remained responsive to evolving conditions. 
Cumulative repo rate cuts, targeted liquidity measures, and 
stronger banking sector balance sheets improved systemic 
liquidity and supported the transmission of lower borrowing 
costs. Together, these measures boosted credit growth and 
created a conducive financing environment for businesses 
and households.

FLUOROPOL YMERS INDUSTRY REVIEW
Fluoropolymers form the backbone of next-generation 
technologies, delivering exceptional thermal stability, 
chemical resistance and dielectric performance that few 
other materials can match. They are indispensable across 
high-growth industries, enabling critical applications such 
as EV battery insulation, green hydrogen electrolyser and fuel 
cell membranes, semiconductor manufacturing, immersion 
cooling for data centres driving artificial intelligence, 
space exploration, advanced medical devices and other  
cutting-edge technologies.
Driven by accelerating demand across these sunrise sectors, 
the global fluoropolymer market is estimated to reach  
US$ 19.3 Billion by 2035, highlighting its growing strategic 
importance in the global advanced materials landscape.
Evolving Industry Dynamics
The fluoropolymers market is transitioning from material 
substitution to performance-driven demand, with growing 
reliance on custom-engineered formulations to meet 
specific thermal, mechanical, and chemical requirements.
Cost structures remain closely linked to monomer availability, 
processing complexity, and stringent quality control 
standards. This has led to margin concentration among 
established players with integrated production capabilities 
and global distribution networks.
Competitive advantage is increasingly defined by control 
over high-performance resin production, formulation 
expertise, and the ability to ensure consistent quality at 
scale. Meanwhile, newer or smaller entrants are focusing on 
niche segments, lean operations, and differentiated service 
offerings to carve out market share.
Sunrise Sectors Driving the Next Wave of Fluoropolymer 
Demand
Electric mobility, semiconductors, solar energy, green 
hydrogen, space exploration and artificial intelligence 
are emerging as the principal growth engines for the 
fluoropolymer industry, collectively representing a US$ 5 
Trillion opportunity by 2035. As these sectors scale globally, 
the demand for advanced fluoropolymer solutions is 
accelerating, driven by the need for superior thermal stability, 
chemical resistance, durability and purity.MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION AND ANAL YSIS REPORT (CONTD.)Corporate Overview Statutory Reports Financial StatementsGujarat Fluorochemicals Limited

systems. Additionally, increasing investments in renewable 
energy infrastructure and sophisticated electronics are 
further strengthening its demand trajectory.

The global fluorochemicals industry is navigating a 
transformative phase, driven by the convergence of

Energy Transition as a Key Growth Driver
The clean energy transition remains a primary catalyst for 
industry growth, with the global renewable power capacity 
reaching approximately 4,500 GW in 2026, signifying a 
robust momentum in decarbonisation. Although bioenergy 
still represents over 50% of total renewable consumption, 
non-bioenergy sources are expected to scale significantly 
from around 6% in 2025 to nearly 16% by 2030 in net-zero 
scenarios. This shift is expected to drive substantial demand 
for fluoropolymers, refrigerants, and specialty materials 
across solar modules, wind turbines, battery systems, and 
hydrogen infrastructure.
Market Size and Growth Outlook
The fluorochemicals market demonstrated steady 
expansion during FY 2025-26, growing from around US$ 
31.4 Billion in 2025 to around US$ 33.4 Billion in 2026. 
Looking ahead, it is projected to reach US$ 55.3 Billion by 
2035, registering a CAGR of about 6.5% over the forecast 
period. Rising demand across diverse industrial applications 
and a growing emphasis on material substitution in favour 
of high-performance fluorinated solutions are powering this 
scale-up.
Product Segment Trends
The fluoropolymers segment, with a share of over 40% 
during the forecast period, is set to retain its dominance 
in the industry. In parallel, specialty fluorochemicals and 
fluorinated gases are gaining traction, particularly in high-
growth applications such as semiconductors, electronics 
manufacturing, and advanced cooling technologies.
Regional Dynamics
Asia-Pacific remains the largest and fastest-growing market 
for fluorochemicals, with projections indicating over 40% 
share in global demand by 2035. Countries such as China 
and India are leading the production and consumption 
landscapes, with sound industrial growth, expanding 
manufacturing ecosystems, and increasing investments 
in infrastructure and renewable energy driving the impetus 
across the region.
Regulatory and Sustainability Landscape
The industry is witnessing increasing regulatory scrutiny, 
particularly concerning environmental impact and 
emissions. This is resulting in a decisive tilt towards sustainable product development, low Global Warming 
Potential (GWP) alternatives, and circularity initiatives. 
Companies are increasingly investing in innovation and 
process optimisation to align with global environmental 
standards while maintaining performance efficiency.
Outlook
The FY 2025-26 marked a period of resilient growth and 
strategic evolution for the fluorochemicals industry. In 
the way ahead, the focus on sustainability, technological 
advancement, and value-added applications will remain 
robust, as demand and regulatory stringency move upward. 
Companies that successfully integrate innovation with 
environmental responsibility are expected to lead the charge.

BULK CHEMICALS INDUSTRY REVIEW
The global bulk chemicals market is in the midst of a 
significant transformation, driven by increasing emphasis on 
sustainability and technological innovation. North America 
remains the largest market, supported by strong industrial 
demand, while Asia-Pacific is the fastest-growing, propelled 
by rapid urbanisation and burgeoning manufacturing 
footprint.
Bulk chemicals serve as essential inputs across industries 
such as pharmaceuticals, plastics, textiles, construction, 
automotive, and electronics. These are broadly classified 
into inorganic and organic segments. Inorganic chemicals 
continue to account for the larger share due to their 
widespread uses, whereas organic chemicals record faster 
adoption for their prevalence in specialised applications.
Market expansion of bulk chemicals is driven by rising end-
user demand and continuous advancements in production 
processes, whereas focus on environmental compliance and 
customisation also add to the momentum. Known for their 
high purity, consistency, and adaptability, these chemicals 
enable efficient, large-scale industrial operations, with 
ongoing innovations further amplifying their performance 
and reliability.

BATTERY CHEMICALS INDUSTRY REVIEW
The global lithium-ion battery market exceeded US$ 
150 Billion in 2025, growing over 20% year-on-year. Its 
significance, however, extends far beyond market size. 
Batteries are now central to electric mobility, enable flexibility 
in power systems, and provide critical backup for data 
centres and AI infrastructure. Beyond energy, they remain 
indispensable across industrial and strategic applications, 
including portable electronics, defence systems, and 
emerging technologies such as robotics. As applications 
expand and costs decline, batteries are fast becoming 
the backbone of modern economies, with wide-ranging 
implications for energy security, industrial competitiveness, 
and policy direction.
Accelerating Demand across Applications
This rising prevalence of lithium-ion battery is reflected 
in deployment trends, with global installations in 2025 
reaching nearly six times 2020 levels. EVs continue to 
dominate demand, accounting for over 70% of total rollout, 
while battery energy storage systems contribute more than 
15%, reflecting their growing importance in maintaining grid 
stability. This trend stands in stark contrast to a decade 
ago, when portable electronics constituted nearly half of global demand. By 2025, their share declined to less 
than 5%, underscoring the rapid diversification of battery 
applications.
Cost Declines Driving Adoption
Falling battery costs continue to drive market expansion. 
In 2025, average prices declined by around 8%, supported 
by manufacturing advances, improved chemistries, and 
intensifying global competition. Battery energy storage 
systems witnessed the steepest decline, with prices 
dropping to nearly one-third of 2020 levels. Lithium iron 
phosphate (LFP) batteries led this trend, with prices falling 
by over 15% compared to less than 5% for lithium nickel 
cobalt manganese (NMC) batteries, making them over 40% 
cheaper on average. They now account for more than half 
of EV batteries and over 90% of energy storage systems 
globally. However, sustained low pricing is placing pressure 
on producers, with several operating at thin or negative 
margins, increasing the likelihood of consolidation.
Regional Disparities and Supply Concentration
The battery market exhibits significant regional disparities, 
with battery pack prices in China approximately 30% lower 
than in the United States and 35% than in Europe. China 
dominates global battery manufacturing, accounting for 
over 80% of production in 2025. In contrast, the United 
States and Europe hold relatively smaller shares and remain 
heavily dependent on imports for critical components. The 
global battery supply chain is also highly concentrated, with 
China, Korea, and Japan producing nearly all lithium-ion 
cells, while China spearheads midstream activities such as 
active materials and precursor manufacturing.
Supply Chain Dependencies and Risks
Heavy reliance on China brings significant supply chain 
vulnerabilities and amplifies concentration risks. This is 
exemplified in the fact that over 70% of EVs produced outside 
China rely on Chinese battery components. Similarly, nearly 
all grid-scale battery systems depend on China at some 
stage of their value chain. Limited investment in midstream 
capabilities in Western markets further compounds these 
risks, highlighting the need for diversified and resilient supply 
chains.
Energy Storage as a Key Growth Driver
Battery energy storage is among the fastest-growing 
segments, with global capacity increasing more than 20-fold 
over the past five years. This growth is driven by declining 
battery costs, expanding renewable deployment, and short 
project timelines. As power systems increasingly rely on 
variable renewables, battery storage is becoming crucial 
for grid stability, flexibility, and resilience, while also creating 
significant commercial opportunities for manufacturers.MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION AND ANAL YSIS REPORT (CONTD.)Corporate Overview Statutory Reports Financial StatementsGujarat Fluorochemicals Limited

their strategic importance is set to grow further. This trend once again emphasises the need for resilient, cost-effective, and 
geographically diversified supply chains as the world gears up for the next phase of energy transition.

Electric Vehicles Industry
The global EV market maintained strong growth in 2025, 
with sales reaching around 20.7 Million units, up 20% year-
on-year. This expansion reflects the accelerating shift 
towards electrified mobility, although growth trends remain 
increasingly uneven across regions. China dominated the 
market with 12.9 Million units, though growth moderated 
due to a high base and evolving subsidy structures, 
prompting manufacturers to expand exports. Europe 
emerged as the fastest-growing major region, recording a 
33% uptick, supported by regulatory mandates and renewed 
consumer incentives, positioning it as a key engine of global 
EV adoption.
In contrast, North America experienced a 4% decline amidst 
policy uncertainty and the withdrawal of incentives. This led 
to greater demand volatility and prompted automakers to 
recalibrate strategies towards hybrid and range-extended 
vehicles. Meanwhile, the Rest of the World grew rapidly by 
154
48%, largely driven by the influx of competitively priced EV 
imports. Growth is expected to moderate in 2026 but remain 
positive, led by Europe and emerging markets, while China 
stabilises and North America faces continued headwinds, 
marking a transition towards a more competitive and policy-
sensitive global EV landscape.

GFL ’s Take
Gujarat Fluorochemicals Limited (GFL) is strengthening its 
presence in the EV battery materials ecosystem through 
its subsidiary, GFCL EV Products Limited. The focus is on 
building India’s first fully integrated battery materials facility. 
The Company has started commercial sales of LiPF6 to 
global customers. The Company has also commissioned its 
electrolyte plant and stabilised its LFP cathode active material 
plant. Among the first commercial-scale facilities outside 
China established by a non-Chinese player, GFCL EV has 
commenced global customer qualification for its products. 
The Company has also successfully qualified its binder 
portfolio with several leading global customers, reinforcing 
its technological capabilities and market acceptance. 
Simultaneously, GFCL EV is expanding its product portfolio 
into critical battery materials, including electrolytes and 
PVDF binders, while advancing next-generation PTFE 
binders to support evolving battery technologies.
To support this growth, GFL secured funding from 
International Finance Corporation and a sovereign fund. It 
is also developing a greenfield battery materials project in 
Oman to sharpen export competitiveness. Backed by a 
planned capex of ~ ₹6,000 Crores over the next 4-5 years, the 
Company is scaling rapidly to address rising demand from 
EV and BESS markets.

domestic manufacturing, upgrading grid infrastructure, and 
integrating energy storage solutions, India is focused on 
expanding its renewable capacity and cementing its role in 
the global solar value chain, supporting long-term energy 
security and sustainability goals.

Hydrogen Fuel Cells and Electrolysers Industry
The global hydrogen and electrolysers market is evolving 
rapidly from a niche technology segment into a central pillar 
of the clean energy transition. The urgent need to elevate 
energy security and decarbonise hard-to-abate sectors 
such as refining, chemicals, and heavy industry is driving 
this change. Electrolysers, which help in producing green 
hydrogen using renewable energy, are gaining increasing 
strategic importance. According to the International Energy 
Agency (IEA), installed electrolyser capacity dedicated to 
hydrogen production reached approximately 1.4 GW by the 
end of 2023. Manufacturing capacity expanded significantly, 
doubling since 2022 to reach nearly 25 GW. With a strong 
project pipeline, global installed electrolyser capacity is 
expected to scale sharply, ranging between 230 GW and 
520 GW by 2030, signalling the growing traction of hydrogen 
technologies.
The market outlook remains highly robust, supported by 
policy incentives, technological advancements, and growing 
corporate decarbonisation commitments. The global 
electrolysers market, valued at over US$ 8.4 Billion in 2025, 
is projected to surge to an estimated US$ 13.2 Billion in 
2026. With an exceptional CAGR of 57.8% during 2026-2035, 
it is expected to reach US$ 509.6 Billion by the end of 2035, 
revealing strong forward drive. Large-scale electrolysers 
(>10 MW) are expected to dominate the market, accounting 
for nearly 76.8% share by 2035, driven by their alignment 
with industrial-scale hydrogen production and national 
energy strategies. Regionally, North America is anticipated 
to lead with a 43.5% market share by 2035, with strong fiscal 
incentives, regulatory support, and tax credits for clean 
hydrogen propelling the progress. Asia-Pacific is projected 
to witness rapid growth as well, driven by rising demand 
across refining and chemical sectors. As renewable energy 
costs decline and power-to-X applications expand, the 
hydrogen economy is set to play a critical role in powering a 
low-carbon, resilient global energy system.
(Source: https://www.researchnester.com/reports/
electrolyzers-market/3485#:~:text=Electrolyzers%20
Market%20Outlook:,by%20the%20end%20of%202023 .)

COMPANY OVERVIEW
Gujarat Fluorochemicals Limited (GFL), a flagship entity of 
the INOXGFL Group, is a global player in fluorine chemistry, 
known for its scale, integration, and technological depth. 
Established in 1987 and headquartered in Noida, the 
Company operates world-class manufacturing facilities in 
Gujarat, supported by a captive fluorspar mine in Morocco 
that secures a stable supply of critical raw materials. Its 
portfolio spans high-performance fluoropolymers such 
as PTFE, PVDF, FKM and FFKM, alongside fluoro-specialty 
chemicals, refrigerants, and industrial chemicals. This 
diverse product profile enables GFL to serve a wide gamut 
of sectors, including pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and 
automotive. Complementing its robust materials platform 
is a sharp focus on environmental stewardship, reflected 
in globally recognised certifications and sustained efforts 
to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, with its initiatives 
acknowledged by the Carbon Disclosure Project (CDP).
Over the past few years, GFL has made a strategic 
transformation from a traditional fluorochemicals 
manufacturer to an innovation-led, future-focused solutions 
provider, rooted in green chemistry. The Company is actively 
building capabilities in next-generation, high-growth 
areas such as EV, BESS, semiconductors, and renewables, 
aligning its business with global decarbonisation and 
energy transition trends. Leveraging cutting-edge R&D and 
precision-driven manufacturing, GFL is delivering future-
ready products to international markets while expanding its 
footprint across India, Europe, and the United States. Firmly 
focused on positioning itself among the world’s leading 
suppliers of fluoropolymers and refrigerants, the Company 
strikes a balance between growth and sustainability, 
solidifying its presence in driving cleaner technologies and 
resilient global supply chains.
DEVELOPMENTS ACROSS OUR BUSINESS SEGMENTS
Fluoropolymers
The Fluoropolymers segment delivered a strong performance 
during the year, with revenue increasing 19% year-on-year, 
driven primarily by higher volumes and supported by price 
increases across key products. Despite a challenging global 
environment, demand remained resilient, underpinned by 
the growing adoption of fluoropolymer solutions in high-
growth sectors such as semiconductors, electric vehicles 
(EVs), battery energy storage systems (BESS), and clean 
energy applications.MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION AND ANAL YSIS REPORT (CONTD.)
156
The long-term outlook for the segment remains highly 
positive, supported by structural growth trends across 
advanced manufacturing and energy transition technologies. 
High-performance fluoropolymers such as PFA and FKM 
are expected to grow at an accelerated pace, driven by 
investments in semiconductor fabrication facilities, AI-
led expansion of data centres, and advanced automotive 
applications. At the same time, emerging opportunities 
in hydrogen, fuel cells, electrolysers, and solar energy 
are expected to strengthen global demand, positioning 
fluoropolymers as a critical enabler of next-generation 
technologies and the transition towards a cleaner energy 
future.
Fluorochemicals
The Fluorochemicals segment delivered a stable 
performance on a year-on-year basis despite a challenging 
global environment and continued weakness in the Middle 
East market. During the year, the business achieved a 
significant milestone with the commencement of R32 
production and sales in March 2026, further strengthening 
its refrigerants portfolio. The segment also remained 
focused on optimising HFC production and undertaking 
incremental capacity expansions to maximise the utilisation 
of its production entitlements under the Kigali Amendment, 
positioning the business to capitalise on evolving global 
refrigerant demand.
The outlook for the business remains favourable, supported 
by disciplined global supply dynamics and healthy 
demand across key end markets, resulting in a positive 
pricing environment for HFCs. Demand for refrigerants is 
expected to remain robust, driven by increasing penetration 
of residential air-conditioning, growth in commercial 
refrigeration, expansion of cold-chain infrastructure, and 
rising investments in cooling infrastructure for AI-driven 
data centres worldwide. These structural demand drivers, 
coupled with opportunities arising from the phased 
implementation of the Kigali Amendment, are expected to 
support the segment’s long-term growth trajectory.
Bulk Chemicals
The Bulk Chemicals segment delivered a steady performance 
during the year, with revenue increasing by 1% on a year-
on-year basis. The business continued to benefit from 
stable demand across key end-use industries, supported 
by its diversified product portfolio and established market 
presence. While operating conditions remained competitive, 
the segment maintained resilience amid evolving market 
dynamics.Looking ahead, the demand outlook for caustic soda is 
expected to remain stable in FY 2026-27. However, pricing 
is likely to remain range-bound owing to ongoing domestic 
capacity additions, which may keep supply-demand 
dynamics balanced. Similarly, the performance of the 
chloromethanes business is expected to remain range-
bound in the near term. Despite these market conditions, 
the segment remains focused on operational efficiency, 
cost optimisation, and maintaining its competitive position 
across core product categories.
Battery Chemicals (GFCL EV)
GFL’s EV-focused subsidiary is rapidly emerging as a key 
growth engine, with commercial supplies of LiPF6 (electrolyte 
salt) commencing in December 2025, thereby positioning 
the Company among a limited number of integrated non-
Chinese producers globally. The successful commissioning 
and stabilisation of its LFP (Lithium Iron Phosphate) 
Cathode Active Material plant, among the first outside China 
by a non-Chinese player, marks a significant milestone, 
with samples already dispatched to global customers. 
PVDF binders are in advanced stages of qualification, 
with commercial operations expected in the first half of  
FY 2026-27. Strengthening its global footprint, GFL 
announced a US$ 216 Million greenfield battery materials 
project in Oman, strategically positioned to leverage Free 
Trade Agreements (FTAs) between the United States and 
India. This growth is further supported by strong capital 
backing, including ₹430 Crores from the International Finance 
Corporation (IFC) and US$ 82 Million from a sovereign fund.
MANUFACTURING STRENGTH AND GLOBAL PRESENCE
GFL’s manufacturing backbone comprises sophisticated, 
integrated facilities in Gujarat, designed to ensure efficiency, 
scale, and product specialisation. While the Ranjitnagar 
plant focuses on specialty chemicals and refrigerants, 
Dahej and Jolva operate as key hubs for fluoropolymers, 
bulk chemicals, and next-generation materials. With sound 
backward integration, the Company boosts operational 
reliability, cost efficiency, and competitive advantage.

OPPORTUNITIES
The global energy and technology landscape is evolving, 
driven by rapid advancements in battery technologies, an 
accelerating, AI-led semiconductor supercycle, and large-
scale deployment of clean energy infrastructure. These 
structural shifts are creating significant opportunities across 
multiple high-growth sectors, strengthening the transition 
towards a low-carbon and digitally enabled global economy.
Battery Demand in Mobility and Storage
Accelerating EV adoption is expected to drive global battery 
demand from around 1 TWh in 2024 to over 3 TWh by 2030. 
Ex-China lithium-ion battery cell demand is projected to 
reach approximately 1.8 TWh by 2030, supported by growing 
EV penetration, expanding energy storage deployments, 
and efforts to localise battery supply chains across North 
America and Europe. This trend is expected to create 
significant opportunities across the battery materials value 
chain.
Global Shift towards LFP Chemistry
LFP chemistry is expected to retain its leadership position 
across mass-market electric vehicle and energy storage 
applications, supported by its cost competitiveness, strong 
safety characteristics, and ability to scale efficiently to meet 
growing demand.
Growing Demand for Battery Energy Storage Systems
Demand for Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) is gaining 
momentum, driven by the rapid growth of AI applications and the expansion of data centre infrastructure, both of which 
require reliable and uninterrupted power supply. At the same 
time, the increasing integration of renewable energy sources 
is creating a greater need for energy storage solutions. By 
enabling efficient energy management and enhancing grid 
reliability, BESS is playing a critical role in stabilising utility 
networks and supporting the transition towards a cleaner 
and more resilient energy ecosystem.
Semiconductor Industry Momentum
The semiconductor industry is on an accelerated trajectory, 
underpinned by rising demand for AI-driven computing, data 
centres, and advanced electronics. Global semiconductor 
revenues grew by approximately 22% year-on-year in 
2025, with scaling up of next-generation technologies 
expected to drive this momentum forward. Despite short-
term challenges such as pricing cycles in memory chips 
and power constraints, the sector remains the core of 
technological progress, with global revenues projected to 
approach the US$ 2 Trillion mark over the next decade.
India’s Solar PV Growth Trajectory
India is steadily bolstering its stature in the global renewables 
landscape. By June 2025, nearly 50% of its installed power 
capacity was derived from non-fossil fuel sources, achieved 
well ahead of its 2030 target. With a long-term ambition 
of reaching 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030, India 
is rapidly expanding utility-scale solar parks alongside 
distributed rooftop initiatives such as PM Surya Ghar: Muft 
Bijli Yojana. These efforts are fortifying energy security and 
domestic manufacturing capabilities.MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION AND ANAL YSIS REPORT (CONTD.)
158
Enabling Deep Decarbonisation
Green hydrogen is emerging as a critical enabler for 
decarbonising hard-to-abate sectors such as steel, shipping, 
and heavy transportation, where direct electrification is not 
feasible. Its high energy density and zero-emission potential 
position it as a viable alternative to fossil fuels, supporting 
global climate goals and industrial transition pathways.
India’s National Green Hydrogen Mission (NGHM)
India’s National Green Hydrogen Mission is gaining steady 
traction, with a target of at least 5 Million metric tonnes 
(MMT) of annual production capacity by 2030. As of 
February 2026, around 8,000 tonnes per annum (TPA) has 
been commissioned, while several large-scale projects are 
underway. The government is strengthening policy support, 
incentive mechanisms, and infrastructure to catalyse 
investments estimated at ₹8 Lakh Crores, with the objective 
of positioning India as a global hub for green hydrogen 
production and exports.

KEY THREATS
The fluorochemicals industry is undergoing a structural 
transformation, shaped by the dual forces: strong demand 
from advanced technology sectors and increasing 
regulatory and operational challenges. As a critical enabler 
for semiconductors, EV battery components, and next-
generation refrigerants, the industry remains integral to 
global technological progress. However, tightening regulatory 
frameworks, particularly evolving PFAS restrictions in 
regions like the European Union, are accelerating the shift 
towards safer, more sustainable manufacturing practices 
and environmentally compliant alternatives.
At the same time, supply chain concentration in key raw 
materials such as fluorspar continues to expose players to 
geopolitical risks and price volatility, while rising energy costs 
and decarbonisation imperatives add further pressure. In 
response, companies are transitioning away from traditional high-volume commodity models towards specialised, 
high-value product portfolios characterised by greater 
traceability, enhanced circularity, and stricter environmental 
standards. Going forward, the ability to innovate beyond 
legacy chemistries and invest in sustainable, high-
performance materials will determine the competitive edge 
for fluorochemical companies in an increasingly regulated 
and sustainability-driven global landscape.
HUMAN RESOURCES
At GFL, people are central to organisational strength and 
treated as a strategic enabler of long-term growth. The 
Company focuses on building an inclusive, agile workforce 
that is adaptive to the evolving industry requirements. 
A structured learning ecosystem is followed to enable 
employees cultivate technical depth, leadership acumen, 
and behavioural competencies, preparing them for larger 
responsibilities and sustained career progression.
Diversity and inclusion are embedded across all people 
practices, ensuring fairness from hiring through to leadership 
development. By encouraging varied perspectives and 
a culture of respect, GFL fosters an environment where 
individuals can contribute authentically. Its policies on 
inclusivity, workplace dignity, and equal opportunity are 
aligned with both regulatory expectations and the Company’s 
broader vision of responsible growth.
The Company places strong emphasis on building 
a connected workforce and enhancing engagement 
through structured platforms that promote dialogue, 
collaboration, and recognition. Leadership interactions, 
team-building initiatives, and performance-linked rewards 
are complemented by transparent communication channels 
and formal feedback systems. This approach ensures that 
employees remain motivated, aligned with organisational 
goals, and confident that their voices are heard. As of  
31st March 2026, GFL’s workforce comprised 3,142 
employees.

  Pursuant to the requirement of the Income-Tax Act, 2025, the Company will be required to withhold taxes at the prescribed 
rates on the dividend paid to its Members.
  To enable the Company to determine the appropriate TDS rate as may be applicable, Members are requested to submit 
the following document(s) and details, as applicable, by e-mail to the Company at vadodara@in.mpms.mufg.com  on or 
before 15th September, 2026 :
A. In case of a Resident Shareholder:
TDS rate Category of shareholder and required documentation
10 per cent with a Valid PAN as per 
Section 393(1) of Income Tax Act, 2025Resident shareholder whose valid Permanent Account Number (‘PAN’) is 
available on records of the Company.
20 per cent without a PAN or Invalid PAN 
or Inoperative PAN as per Section 397 of
